title: node/switch
description: Route to exactly one node. Rules are tried in order over this node's inputs; the first that holds names the node that runs, else the fallback; a `catch` routes a named node's fault. Every other candidate, and everything reachable only through it, is cancelled. Expressions: has(path), comparisons, && || !, len(x).

type.description: Marks this node a switch: it routes to exactly one node.

description.description: What this node decides, for a reader of the graph.

label.description: A short human name for this node, shown wherever a reader sees it instead of its id.

rules.description: The rules, tried in order over this node's inputs. The first that holds names the node that runs.

when.description: The condition, an expression over this node's inputs that must answer a boolean (G011).

description.description: What this rule decides, for a reader of the graph.

catch.description: The nodes whose fault this switch routes, and where each goes: when a node named here breaks -- its handler threw something that is not a refusal, the graph it ran broke, its timeout struck -- the run goes on, this switch routes to the node named for it as if a rule had held, and the rules and `else` are not tried. A refusal is never caught. A node named here is one this switch reads (G021), and everything else that reads it is routed by this switch (G022); the node routed to reads nothing of it (G023). Only a data graph catches (L013), and only an effect can be caught (G024).
